    Historical and continuing regional connection

    Previously inspected report concerns Ahtna Copper River regional history in Alaska. Public regional association only; no sensitive places or exact territorial geometry.

    Historical and continuing homeland connection

  • Tlingit↗Historical homeland / community government connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland / community government connection

    The Council's timeline explicitly identifies Tlingit and Haida as distinct nations and repeatedly locates the historical land-use and claims account in Southeast Alaska. Supports Alaska for the Tlingit directory entry; this joint Council does not stand for every Tlingit community or the full cross-border homeland.

    Historical Southeast Alaska geography in the joint Council's public timeline. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Connection & source
    Documented language community geography

    The university profile explicitly locates Central Yup'ik people on Alaska's western central coast. This concerns Central Alaskan Yup'ik rather than every Yupik language; conflicting and dated speaker totals are not adopted.

These are starting lists, not a complete census. Modern borders help you navigate; they are not Indigenous homeland boundaries. A connection may be historical or present-day and does not imply presence throughout a region. Directory names can overlap; the profiles explain their relationships.
